purpose: Turn Cook County assessed values into the Assessor's market value: market value = assessed value / level of assessment.

1.label: vacant
1.source: Assessor class definitions (2018): Major Class 1 Vacant, 10%

2.label: residential, 1-6 units
2.source: Assessor class definitions (2018): Major Class 2 Residential, 10%

3.label: multifamily, 7+ units
3.source: Classification ordinance: 10% for residential, vacant and apartment property (Civic Federation, 2008)

4.label: not for profit
4.source: Assessor class definitions (2018): Major Class 4 Not For Profit, 20%

5.label: commercial or industrial
5.source: Assessor class definitions (2018): Major Class 5A Commercial and 5B Industrial, 25%

6.label: industrial incentive
6.source: Assessor class definitions (2018): 6B, 10% for the first 10 years

7.label: commercial incentive
7.source: Assessor class definitions (2018): 7B, 10% for the first 10 years, then 15% and 20%

8.label: commercial or industrial incentive
8.source: Assessor class definitions (2018): 8, 10% for the first 10 years

notes: Incentive classes step up after year 10, so a value from the 10% level can overstate market value for an older incentive; the screen says so.
Mixed-use class 3-18 buildings are split by the Assessor (residential part at 10%, commercial part at 25%); the class on the row decides the level here.
Stage order, best first: board (Board of Review final), certified (Assessor after appeals), mailed (first notice).

sales_ratio_check.method: 2025 Board of Review market value / sale price, single-parcel warranty and trustee sales 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-31, Assessor sale filters applied
sales_ratio_check.reading: Assessor values run below recent sale prices (class 2: 14% below at the median). Show the Assessor value as the Assessor's figure, not as a price.
